quandoUsar: A long, dense time series where the user needs the whole history and a close look at any stretch.
Mark events in the series (launches, price changes) with `annotations` and read each one on the chart itself.
Sync the window with shortcuts or other panels, through `range` and `onRangeChange`.
quandoEvitar: Use `line-chart` to compare more than one series: here there is only one.
Use `bar-chart` for a few periods compared one by one and against the average.
Use `sparkline` for a compact trend next to a number.

teclado.acao: Goes through four stops: the chart, the overview strip window, the start handle, and the end handle.
On the chart, move the reading to the previous point, the next, the first, and the last visible point.
On the window, shift the range by 10% of its width; on a handle, move that edge one point; with `Shift`, the step becomes 50% or ten points.
On the chart, jump about one eighth of the visible points; on the window and handles, take the large step.
With focus on the window, zoom in (half the range) or out (double).
On the window or handles, return to the whole series; on the chart, `Esc` clears the reading.

acessibilidade: The chart is a focusable group that announces the date and value of the point being read in an `aria-live` region; a hidden table carries the points and events of the current window.
The window and the two handles are `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext` in dates, and each one is a `Tab` stop.
`label` is required; the group instruction, the handle names, and the axis dates are in English in the code (`formatDate` only changes the tooltip and announcements).
movimento: The line draws from left to right the first time it appears; on zoom in, the value axis adjusts with a spring to the highest point in the window.

The window follows the finger with no delay while dragging and slides with a spring when `range` changes externally or when it returns to the whole series; the tooltip follows the crosshair with a spring.
With “reduce motion”, the line already appears whole, the window and axis jump to the destination, and the tooltip follows without a spring.
responsivo: It measures its own width: date labels move from days to weeks, months, quarters, and years depending on space, and event labels that would collide are hidden.
Chart and strip use `touch-action: pan-y`, so dragging vertically keeps scrolling the page; heights come from `height` (240) and `overviewHeight` (52), in pixels.
desempenho: Above two points per pixel the line keeps only the minimum and maximum of each column; the hidden table, however, has one row per point in the window, so aggregate very long series before passing them.
Keep `data` and `annotations` with a stable reference (`useMemo`): smoothing and the overview strip are recalculated whenever they change.
notasIA: `data` is `{ date, value }` with `date` as a `Date` or milliseconds, in ascending order; with fewer than two points `emptyLabel` appears, and the value axis always starts at zero.

`range` is a target, not a lock: the window moves on its own while dragging and only slides when `range` changes, so keep what comes from `onRangeChange` in state; without `range`, use `defaultRange`.
The component assumes one point per day: when zoomed out the line becomes a seven-point average with a band, and the tooltip compares with seven points earlier, calling it “a week earlier”.
